Data:End.h.sky.oldl.json.label: The Winds of Noon
Data:End.h.sky.oldl.json.Desc: This History is my last and greatest work. That old lost music will draw the Birds, the Names, the architects and the adepts to Noon across the evening sea. 'Noon, they say, is not as it was.' But Noon, with its towers of ivory, its wheels of shining iron, is becoming something more. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.sky.oldl.magnate.json.label: Magnate Victory: Peace at Noon
Data:End.h.sky.oldl.magnate.json.Desc: I've found my peace. That old lost music will draw the Birds, the Names, the architects and the adepts to Noon across the evening sea. Port Noon, across the evening sea. It's long been a place for Long, and now it's something more. Each day more of us arrive. The waves take our name as once the fountain did. The towers rise day by day. Here in the City's shade, there will be peace. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.sky.oldl.symurgist.json.label: Symurgist Victory: Songs at Noon
Data:End.h.sky.oldl.symurgist.json.Desc: My songs await me. That old lost music will draw the Birds, the Names, the architects and the adepts to Noon across the evening sea. Across the evening sea to Noon - for so long a city of Long, and now a city of song. Each day the ivory towers rise a little higher. 'Noon, they say, is not as it was.' But now we hear on the wind what Noon could become. I have found that old lost music… and the Hours of the Roost take up the refrain. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.sky.unde.json.label: The Last City, Noon
Data:End.h.sky.unde.json.Desc: This History is my last and greatest work. This will be the last city on Earth. When it passes, so will the world. Across the evening sea. Ever since the Spring of the Witness rose from the earth, Port Noon has been a place for the ones who defy endings. Now, as the ivory towers rise, it's a place for those who accept them. In the end, that'll be all of us. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.sky.unde.magnate.json.label: Magnate Victory: Silence at Noon
Data:End.h.sky.unde.magnate.json.Desc: I've found my peace. This will be the last city on Earth. When it passes, so will the world. 'The houses are white and the hills are green and the air is golden and the sea won’t settle on one colour….' That's still true. But all the colours grow pale. The towers of ivory will rise higher day by day. One day, they'll be complete. Until then, I'll know peace; and when they're complete, it won't matter any more. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.bala.executioner.json.label: Executioner Victory: Robin in the Snow
Data:End.h.winter.bala.executioner.json.Desc: This is the History where the travelling-kinds of the Carapace Cross return… and everything changes. What is above, below; what has wings, shall thrive. And I'll have made amends. The Carapace Cross is gone. Into earth; into flesh; and the travelling-kinds,beyond wave and sky. They are very few now under the earth, and the Cross-in-flesh are us - some of us, at least. But when the travelling-kinds return, their wings will darken the sky; and in this history, they will be safe from any Dawn. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.bala.json.label: Closing a Wound
Data:End.h.winter.bala.json.Desc: This is the History where the travelling-kinds of the Carapace Cross return… and everything changes. What is above, below; what has wings, shall thrive. The Cross died not but passed within.' When the travelling-kinds of the Carapace Cross return, how many of us will answer the heart-lifting buzz of their call? One in every thousand? One in every ten? There will be no Second Dawn - the Cross will walk among us - and when the wing-buzz, the heart-shrill, the star-song, goes out, when we are called to travel again beyond the sky - how many of us will go with them? -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.bala.revolutionary.jso.label: Revolutionary Victory: Frost
Data:End.h.winter.bala.revolutionary.jso.Desc: There will be no Second Dawn. This is the History where the travelling-kinds of the Carapace Cross expose the lies of the Church… and the roots of Calyptra will tremble. Safe from any Second Dawn - In streets at night - in spires by day - crawling on the roofs of moving trains - buzzing in factory chimneys - the kinds of the Cross return. Of course they'll frighten the wits out of everyone - everyone! But the Calyptra's law doesn't bind the Cross. When they're ready to speak, and we're ready to listen - to the hybrids in our sky, and the echo in our flesh - the tyranny of Eternity, at long last, will approach its resolution. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.conf.archaeologist.jso.label: Archaeologist Victory: A Cage of Stars
Data:End.h.winter.conf.archaeologist.jso.Desc: There will be no Second Dawn. The adepts of this History will make a prison for the sharpest lights, the most perilous fires... and for my other self. At last I will be free. This is the cell the Watchman built for the Wolf-Divided, in the southmost reaches of the world, where the sea grows hard as horn and the sunset pale as snow. When the sunset comes, it will be his cell. Without the Wolf, we will see no Second Dawn. There may - there just may - be other benefits beside. No more Wolf-Splinters, for one. Is that my shadow? Or is it, finally, me? Let's say it's not. Let's say I'm free.. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.conf.json.label: A Cage of Snows
Data:End.h.winter.conf.json.Desc: There will be no Second Dawn. The adepts of this History - my last and greatest work - will make a prison for the sharpest lights, the most perilous fires... and the kindling-spark that might have been the Dawn. This is the cell the Watchman built in the southmost reaches of the world, where the sea grows hard as horn and the sunset pale as snow. When the sunset comes, it will be his cell. Without the Watchman, there will be no Second Dawn. 'He navigates; he illuminates; he is not compassionate...' Perhaps when night falls, we'll finally see a little compassion. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.conf.prodigal.json.label: Prodigal Victory: A Cage of Visions
Data:End.h.winter.conf.prodigal.json.Desc: There will be no Second Dawn. The adepts of this History will make a prison for the sharpest lights, the most perilous fires.. I will be safe at last. This is the cell the Watchman built in the southmost reaches of the world, where the sea grows hard as horn and the sunset pale as snow. When the sunset comes, it will be his cell. Without the Watchman, there will be no Second Dawn… and without the Watchman, my pursuers will lose their force. A little light in the world is a small price to pay. After all, without the Watchman, there'll be a little more mercy, too. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.unde.json.label: The Lights Along The Way
Data:End.h.winter.unde.json.Desc: Husher foresaw the long road to silence, and the lights along the way. This History is my last and greatest work; and in it there will be no Second Dawn. Julian Coseley, the anarchist, Eternity's enemy. What convinced him, in the end, that Husher had any kind of point? The paradox of the eternal ending? The colours too pale for sight? Was it the secrets he saw in Ninegala's paintings? His defeats? The quenching of his arrogance? Or just the length of his long long life? Why Silence? If that's a question, Silence always has an answer. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.h.winter.unde.magnate.json.label: Magnate Victory: The Whitest Flower
Data:End.h.winter.unde.magnate.json.Desc: There need be no Second Dawn. All the colours of the world are enough. In that understanding I will find my peace. 'Speech is a wound,' Husher famously insisted. Of silence, he said nothing at all. But then, of course, I suppose, he wouldn't. It's enough. I'm tired. What is written is written, and my contribution comes after this mark. -- [You have proved yourself as Librarian; convinced the Hours to accept a History; changed the world; won the game. This is the memory that does not die. Please accept our congratulations.]

Data:End.hol.institute.autarchy.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Autarchy
Data:End.hol.institute.autarchy.json.desc: The institute stands for all humanity, but first of all it stands for continuity… and before anything else, this must mean the continuity of the Institute. So while the War in the Sun ravaged the invisible world, and the War in the World ravaged Europe, the Institute husbanded its resources and deployed them judiciously - protecting a site of interest here, a looted collection there. Now that the wars are past, the Institute has staked a claim to a hidden Alpine valley, where it protects those it finds sufficiently interesting, and builds its plans for the future: a brighter, wider world beyond the reach of the Ministries of the Gleam-touched East, the Coronal Incorporates of the West. But the Institute's root and heart remains Hush House, the fortress of knowledge where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every cliff a fortress; every hermitage a mountain.']

Data:End.hol.institute.better.gods.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Better Gods
Data:End.hol.institute.better.gods.json.desc: The Wars, above and below, ravaged the waking world, the Mansus, and the Sun… and the Institute seized the opportunity. Following the strategy of a capricious, visionary immortal - not without misgivings - they worked with the Crown, with rebellious Forge-long, with the Gleam-touched, to construct surrogate Hours. With so many Hours now uncounted in the war, their timing could not have been better. Their surrogates have brought stability to a shattered Europe. But they have not been exactly loyal to the Institute, and the Institute remains in the background. But the background is where all its members are most comfortable; not least the Librarian, who, silent before the sunset glimmerings of the Brancrug sea, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every flame has its fuel; every fuel fears its flame.']

Data:End.hol.institute.corrivality.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Corrivality
Data:End.hol.institute.corrivality.json.desc: The Institute set itself to feed the conflicts that feed the world… and the world went up like naphtha beneath an open flame. It was inevitable; the Institute's provocations were one cause among a hundred; and if some of the founders regret their part, still the War in the World and the War in the Sun made for unimaginable opportunities - profits both visible and invisible. In the ruins of the new Europe, the Institute is a hidden power, carving out its own domain between other spheres of influence - the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West, the Gleam-touched Ministries of the East. Much has changed since its birth at Hush House - but Hush House still stands, under the Institute's protection, and there the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Only twins drown twice.']

Data:End.hol.institute.peace.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Peace
Data:End.hol.institute.peace.json.desc: The Institute could not prevent the coming war, any more than a lighthouse could prevent a storm. And so the storm broke, on Europe and the world. But how many bodies did they save? And how many souls? Through the falls of the Stars and the rise of the Incorporates, through all the plagues of Worm and amber, the Institute built havens, found time and strength for its guests to build bridges. And the oldest, the kindest, the strongest of those havens was Hush House... where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Silence after lightning; silence before thunder.']

Data:End.hol.institute.revelation.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Revelation
Data:End.hol.institute.revelation.json.desc: The Institute at its founding resolved to undermine Calyptra. Its founders never guessed how successful they could be. The War in the Sun brought an end to the established order. With so many Hours uncounted or fled - with the horrors of the old spirits and the new weapons ravaging Europe - with the Gleam-touched Ministries rising in the East, and the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West - the laws of secrecy crumbled. The Institute set itself to guarding knowledge and guiding its seekers. And the centre of that endeavour remains - of course - Hush House: where the Librarian, as always, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every lighthouse needs a lamp at the top and rocks at the bottom.'']

Data:End.hol.institute.secrecy.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Secrecy
Data:End.hol.institute.secrecy.json.desc: The Institute at its founding resolved to protect the daylight world from the dangers of the invisible arts - even if that meant upholding the tyranny of Calyptra. Its founders never guessed how challenging that would be. The War in the Sun brought an end to the established order. With so many Hours uncounted or fled - with the horrors of the old spirits and the new weapons ravaging Europe - with the Gleam-touched Ministries rising in the East, and the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West - it was impossible to maintain the laws of secrecy. The Institute set itself to the protection of the most dangerous knowledge, and the education of its seekers. And the centre of that endeavour remains - of course - Hush House: where the Librarian, as always, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Rocks are no sharper in the dark.']

Data:End.hol.institute.stone.consumed.js.label: The Lighthouse Institute: Stone Consumed
Data:End.hol.institute.stone.consumed.js.desc: Through the years of the War in the World and the War in the Sun, the Institute shattered prehuman altars in search of secrets, excavated the corpses of primordial colossi to render them to wisdom. The caution of the old Curia and of the Obliviates had given way to a new ruthlessness. They emerged as one of the hidden powers of the new Europe, treating profitably with the Gleam-touched Ministries and Glory-gifted Incorporates. From the shadows, they helped guide the continent back towards the light... and in the shadows, the lights of Hush House still glow across the water, and the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Many pebbles, one Beach.']

Data:End.hol.institute.stone.remembered..label: The Lighthouse Institute: Stone Remembered
Data:End.hol.institute.stone.remembered..desc: The Institute in silence unearthed the secrets of the Hours that came before. When War came to the Mansus and the Wake, they preserved those secrets for an uncertain future. They learnt of their predecessors: the ones who had been called the Obliviates, and their nameless precursors who had served the same role beneath a redder sun. And so the Institute became another fire-forged link in the wisdom-chain that runs into the dawn. Knowledge endures; books are the memory that does not die; and nowhere is this more true than at Hush House, where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'The waves leave what the world's lost.']

Data:End.hol.institute.uncertain.json.label: The Lighthouse Institute: An Uncertain Mission
Data:End.hol.institute.uncertain.json.desc: The Institute never found a clear mission, beyond the preservation of its own privacy and the advancement of its members' interests. But through the War in the World and the War in the Sun, as Europe convulsed and the skies wrung out their cargo of blood and Stars, the Institute remained, persisted, endured, in the shadow of the long traditions of the Obliviates and of the Curia of the Isle; through all that time, the Librarian remained at Hush House and kept their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Hush House endures; the Institute persists']

Data:End.u.evening.json.label: Evening Falls
Data:End.u.evening.json.desc: Hush House lives again. Perhaps that's all I want. Some of the very best Librarians have worked well, lived quietly, left the world a better place... I have my fire, my books, my clock, my window on the world where they do other things; and I am happy. This is the life I chose. The years will pass, like sun, like snow, like rain, like a gull's wing beating, and when I close my eyes, they will find me smiling. -- [You have completed the game: congratulations. Greater victories are available, but there is an argument to be made that this is the best ending of BOOK OF HOURS.]

Data:End.u.winter.json.label: A Knowledge In The Look Of Things
Data:End.u.winter.json.desc: January 9th, 1838. A heavy snow falls on Brancrug. When the staff dig themselves out, Solomon Husher, third Librarian of the House, has disappeared from his quarters in the Long Tower, leaving a letter of resignation. 'Winter,' the letter concludes, 'does not wait forever; though Janus might.' Husher is never seen again, but every year on the same day, his footprints can be found beneath the Tree. After the red leaf and the gold have gone, Brought down by the wind, then by hammering rain... ...I speak to you now with the land's voice, It is the cold, wild land that says to you A knowledge glimmers in the sleep of things: The old hills hunch before the north wind blows. - Howard Nemerov, 1920-1991, from 'A Spell Before Winter'. -- [You have completed a hidden ending. An argument has been made that this is the true ending of BOOK OF HOURS.]

Data:Essence.iotic.json.Label: Iotic Essence
Data:Essence.iotic.json.Desc: 'In the later operations of the Forge, the Madrugad yields to the true Forge of Days, and the essence begins to redden.' The bit about the 'true Forge of Days' nearly got St Melancthe burned for heresy, but no-one ever said she was wrong about the second part.

xexts.scrutiny: Redder than sunset. [A range of Forge recipes can be used to create Iotic Essence from a range of precursors.]

Data:Essence.xanthotic.json.Label: Xanthotic Essence
Data:Essence.xanthotic.json.Desc: The rich gold of a summer afternoon. 'If sunlight precedes moonlight,' St Anselm observed, 'the Meniscate must precede the Madrugad; and the light that was lost will remain.'

xexts.scrutiny: Yellower than buttercups. [Various Lantern recipes can be used to create Xanthotic Essence from various precursors.]

Data:Essential.periost.json.Label: Essential Periost
Data:Essential.periost.json.Desc: What happens when you boil and scrape us down to our utter fundamentals.

xexts.scrutiny: This was something left from before any of us were born - from a time when the sun swung red and low -   [There are Nectar, Moon and Winter recipes which can be used to craft this from mortal remains.]

Data:Evas.locks.json.Label: Eva's Locks
Data:Evas.locks.json.Desc: A pale wrack washed up on the beach by Brancrug.

xexts.scrutiny: Named for Lady Eva, who drowned herself with her grandchildren after the death of Sebastian her nephew. Her motives were never clear; her body, and the bodies of her grandchildren, were never found.
